reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown read Joshua's long day as poetic, prolonged light rather than an actual halt in the sun's motion, leaving Genesis's promised day-night cycle intact.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Baruch Spinoza argued the narrative asserts a literal halt of the sun and moon, reflecting the Israelites' geocentric worldview rather than an actual event.

sides.snippet: day and night shall not cease
sides.verseText: While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.\"

sides.snippet: The sun stayed in the midst of the sky, and didn't hurry to go down about a whole day.
sides.verseText: The sun stood still, and the moon stayed, Until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn't this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stayed in the midst of the sky, and didn't hurry to go down about a whole day.
